days.label: Friday
days.text: Friday runs from lunch straight through last call. Baby Fearn plays the free lunchtime set in City Hall Park at 12:30, and the Heineberg Chicken BBQ serves chicken off the grill on the senior center lawn at 11:30 for folks 60 and up, tickets required and it sells out every year. After work, the South Burlington Farmers Market sets up along the airport rec path from 5 to 7, the South End Get Down brings food trucks and DJs to Coal Collective on Pine Street from 5 to 9, and Food Truck Friday at Sisters of Anarchy in Shelburne has the Grace Palmer Band and Nameless Tacos from 5. Spare Time Colchester is throwing a Heroes Appreciation Night from 6 to 8 with free bowling and shoes for first responders, healthcare workers and military, RSVP on their page. Bar Renée hosts A Hot New Jersey Night from 6 with pork roll sandwiches, a Jersey vintage pop up and live music from 7, and the Crochet with Cats ($45) workshop at Queen City Cat Lounge teaches a catnip toy from 6 to 8 with adoptable cats underfoot. Moms, the Mom Prom: Tropical Paradise ($69.99) cruise sails Friday evening on the Spirit of Ethan Allen with dinner and a live DJ, and if you would rather walk the waterfront, the sunset walk and creemee stroll [MEETUP] meets behind ECHO at 7 for an easy loop to the Sweet Spot.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday is a big one. Our own BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] holds holds it down at Zero Gravity at 10, grab a coffee and come say hi, and apparently right next to us the Junior League pours coffee and waffles at the Zero Gravity beer hall from 10. Right down the street, the Burlington Farmers Market runs 9 to 2 at 345 Pine Street. The Colchester Conservation Commission leads an invasive species walk through the St. Michael's natural area from 10 to noon, and the new BHS/BTC campus throws its grand opening block party on Institute Road from 11 to 2 with a ribbon cutting, pizza, bounce houses and self guided tours. Two festivals kick off at noon. First African Landing Day fills the Intervale Center from 12 to 5 with food, music, drumming and speakers commemorating the 1619 arrival of the first Africans in the English colonies, and Burlington Electric's Net Zero Energy Festival moves to Waterfront Park this year from 12 to 4 with e-bike test rides, an EV showcase, induction cooking demos and Sambatucada at 3. A Winooski neighbor is throwing a block party at the end of North Street from 1 to 5 with a bounce house and a piñata, bring a dish. Readers can join the Helm book club [MEETUP] at Zero Gravity at 2, and the Lake Champlain Chamber Music Festival opens at Elley-Long in Colchester with a 2 PM Spotlight concert with Ignat Solzhenitsyn followed by a conversation about his family's journey from the Soviet Union to Vermont. If you want to be on the water instead, a river float on the Winooski [Forever 38 MEETUP] meets at Volunteers Green in Richmond at 1, bring your own float.

days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday afternoon and night keep going. The Summer BBQ and Backpack Giveaway at Essex Alliance's North Avenue campus runs 4 to 7 with burgers, yard games and live music, rain or shine. The 2026 Vermont Reggae Fest ($75-$85) takes over the Main Street Landing meadow on the waterfront with doors at 3 and music from 4, Richie Spice, Sister Nancy, The Abyssinians and Marlon Asher on the bill, and Foam keeps it going with a free after party with Channel Two Dub Band at 10. City Hall Park's free Twilight Series has April Patterson Clemens and Cobalt Tolbert at 6 and Night Protocol at 7:30. Tank Recording Studio hosts Songwriters in the Round , a live recording session with the LCES songwriter competition winners, doors at 6:30 and music at 7. Gary Gulman does 7 and 9:30 shows at Vermont Comedy Club, Debí Tirar Más Fiestas turns the Higher Ground Ballroom into a Latin dance night at 9 with a portion of proceeds to Migrant Justice, and Moonbird plays a free set at On Tap in Essex Junction at 9.

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday gets its business done before the rain. Duo Dolce , two Vermont Symphony players, give a free Sunday Classical program at the BCA Center at 10, and the First UU holds its Blessing of the Animals on the lawn at the top of Church Street from 10 to 11:15, leashes, carriers, stuffies and photos all welcome. The Friends of the South Burlington library trade donuts for fiction donations in the library foyer from 10 to 1. The Vermont Italian Cultural Association's annual picnic is a potluck at Oakledge's upper pavilion from 12 to 3, fifth generation farmer Mike Isham reads from his new book of farm stories at Isham Family Farm in Williston at 2, and the Silent Book Club reads companionably on Hotel Vermont's covered terrace from 2 to 4, rain or shine. The chamber music festival's first mainstage concert, 'From the Motherland' , is at Elley-Long at 3 with a pre concert conversation first. Overconsumption Thrifts hosts a Girls Day Out pop up at specs in Winooski from 4 to 9 with eight vendors, two DJs, tarot and henna. Sunday night, Hidden Brain's Shankar Vedantam brings the podcast to the Flynn Main Stage at 6, the Candlelight Rest & Renewal yin and yoga nidra session runs 6 to 8 at 100 Church Street with preregistration required, and the Latin Dance Night ($59.99) cruise sails Sunday evening on the Spirit of Ethan Allen with an hour of lessons and 90 minutes of open dancing. Old Spokes Home screens Best Day Ever , a documentary about two adaptive mountain bikers, in its lot with doors at 7 and the film at 7:30, free with donations welcome. Higher Ground closes the weekend with Mad Caddies in the Showcase Lounge with doors at 7 and Morgan Wade in the Ballroom at 8.
